get.summary: List or search the cards
get.description: Cards read in creation order, oldest first, so a walk never skips a card that moves between columns. `q` narrows the walk and does not rank it. Terminal columns are included.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most rows to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque position from the `next` URL of the last page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The walk order. A leading `-` is descending. `createdAt` is the same order as `number`, because a number counts up in creation order.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search words, in the title and the body of every card. Matching is by substring, ignoring case. Every word must match. Quote a phrase, prefix `-` to exclude, and write `or` for either. `12` or `#12` also finds that card.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only cards in the column with this slug.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only cards of this type key.

parameters.name: reporter
parameters.description: Only cards raised by this reporter.

parameters.name: parentCardId
parameters.description: Only the children of the card with this id.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Only the children of the card with this number. Do not pass it with `parentCardId`.

parameters.name: paused
parameters.description: True for only the cards with an active pause, and false for only those with none.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only cards whose state is of this kind. A card shows one state, the first of its reasons, and this filter reads that one. A card in a terminal column has no state, so `status=done&state=working` answers an empty list. A card that enters or leaves the state during a walk can be missed, as with `status` and `paused`. One kind per request.

parameters.name: stateCode
parameters.description: Only cards whose state has this code, such as `run-open` for a running worker. The codes belong to the workflow of the project, so a code that no state has answers an empty list. Pass it with `state` to narrow a kind.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: The fields to return, as a comma list such as `number,title`. Each named field comes back whole, and nothing else does. `all` returns the whole resource and stands alone.

delete.summary: Lift the workflow pause of a card
delete.description: The workflow pauses a card when a rule used up its retries or its work limit, or when a worker stopped with a refusal that the workflow does not retry. Lift a pause only when its cause is gone. A pause of kind `rule` ends only on its own release condition. This call differs from the hold route, which makes a card unmanaged.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The card number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project.

parameters.name: pauseId
parameters.description: Lift this pause only, so a pause that changed since you read it is refused. Leave it out to lift the active pause.

put.summary: Put the columns in a new order
put.description: Backlog always comes first and never moves, so leave it out. `errors[].code` is `backlog_in_order`, `unknown_column` or `order_incomplete`.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

200.description: Every column, in the new order.

post.summary: Place a block of cards in one column
post.description: The listed cards form one block, in list order, at the place. The other cards keep their order around it. The call changes ranks only: every listed card must already sit in the column, and a terminal column refuses the call. The whole call is refused or applied: nothing changes on a 422. A rank change starts no workflow work and writes no history row. `errors[].code` is `place_missing`, `place_conflict`, `unknown_column`, `terminal_column`, `list_empty`, `card_listed_twice`, `card_unknown`, `card_not_in_column`, `neighbour_in_list` or `neighbour_not_in_column`.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

200.description: The placed block and the cards just above and below it.

They describe the whole machine, so they cover every run on that bridge in that window, not only this run. A bridge sends samples only when the instance flag `bridge.host_sampling_enabled` is on and its rule file does not set `collect: false`, so a run can have none. `note` says why the list is empty when the run has no bridge or no start.

get.summary: List the worker runs
get.description: The runs of the project, the run whose first report came last first. A worker run is one run of a bridge worker on one subject, which is usually a card. A filter narrows the list, and all filters apply together. `endedAfter` and `endedBefore` are inclusive and read the end of a run, or the time of its first report for a run with no end. A date with no time reads as midnight UTC, and a time with no offset reads as UTC. Each row carries the figures of the run: its usage, its model and its metrics. `GET .../runs/{run}` reads one run in full. The state of the project can change between two pages of a walk, so a run that arrives meanwhile can be missed.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most rows to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque position from the `next` URL of the last page.

parameters.description: Only runs in one of these states, such as failed, gave-up, blocked, timed-out or lost. Repeat the parameter, or separate the states with commas.

parameters.name: card

parameters.name: account

parameters.name: model

parameters.name: endedBefore

parameters.name: q

post.description: Asks the bridge of a run to resume it. A resume continues the session of the run as a new run of the same series. The command waits for the bridge, which resumes the run when it reads the command, and the run list then shows it as `pendingCommand`. Only a run in the state blocked, gave-up, failed, no-result, unfinished, timed-out, lost, stopped or waiting-for-person can resume. A resume by an API key records the key on the command. `POST .../runs/resume` resumes up to 50 runs.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: run
parameters.description: The id of a worker run of the project, from the run list.

post.description: Asks the bridge of each run to resume it, each run on its own and in order, so a refused run does not stop the others. The answer is 200 with one row per run id, in the order of the request, so read each row: the status does not show the outcome of a run. A run of another project gets the row `not-found`, as a missing run does. An unexpected failure on a run gives the row `error`, whose outcome is unknown, and the route then stops: each later row is `not-attempted`. Send those runs again. A resume by an API key records the key on each command.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

get.description: The headline, the variants and the metrics that the Comparison tab shows. The cards stay on `GET .../experiments/{experiment}/cards`. `confidenceLevel` is the level of every range: 0.95 for one comparison or none, and 1 - 0.05 / N for N comparisons. A money value is in US dollars, a duration of a built-in metric in milliseconds, a duration of a metric that the workflow template declares in hours, and a ratio is between 0 and 1.

Archiving an archived experiment moves its archive time forward, and restoring one that is not archived changes nothing.

parameters.name: experiment

get.summary: Read one worker run in full
get.description: The run with its output and its state changes, every run of its series, and every command that a person, an agent or an API key sent to a bridge for a run of the series. A series starts with one run, and each resume of a run starts a new run that continues it. When an older run was deleted, its continuations lose their link to it, and the series lists only the branch of the oldest run that remains. The tool calls and the host samples have their own routes.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: run
parameters.description: The id of a worker run of the project, from the run list.

200.description: The run, its series and its commands.

post.description: Asks the bridge of a queued, resumed, preparing or running run to stop it. The command waits for the bridge, which stops the run when it reads the command, and the run list then shows it as `pendingCommand`. A stop ends this run only. It does not make the card unmanaged, so a bridge rule can still start new work on it. PUT the card hold for that. An interactive session closes in Loupe at once and answers `closed` with no `commandId`, because no bridge holds it. A stop by an API key records the key on the command, and on the closed session.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: run
parameters.description: The id of a worker run of the project, from the run list.

200.description: The stop is requested, or the session is closed.

parameters.name: path

post.summary: Put an item in the inbox of the owner
post.description: Hands one question, to-do or notice to the owner of the project, who answers it in the Loupe inbox. Nothing waits on the item, so `blocking` is always false, and the owner can dismiss any item. With `dedupeKey`, a call returns the open item that holds the same key with 200 and creates nothing. `Location` names the item. Read the answer with `getInboxItem`. The item names the API key that made it.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your choice. A retry with the same key and body answers as the first request did. The same key with another body gets 409 `idempotency_key_reused`.

200.description: The open item that already holds the `dedupeKey`. Nothing was created.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

url.description: The Feedback tab of its card in the app, scrolled to the note. Null when the note has no card.

pageUrl.description: The page of the reviewed site where a web note was left, or null for a native note.

screenshot.description: The size of the marked image of the note, or null.

hasDrawing.description: True when the note has strokes. Ask the reviewer rather than guess.

context.description: What a preview page said it served, or null.

PartialArtifact.description: Some of the fields of `Artifact`, each one whole. A field that the request does not name is absent.

url.description: The artifact page in the app, at the newest version. It needs a sign-in. `pageLink` needs none.

selectedVersion.description: The version whose files are listed.

pageLink.description: A full address of the entry page of that version, valid for one hour, or null when the version has none.

PartialCard.description: Some of the fields of `Card`, each one whole. A field that the request does not name is absent.

url.description: The card page in the app.

number.description: The short label that counts from 1 inside this project.

type.description: A type key of the project.

position.description: The rank inside the column, counting from 0.

state.description: The last state Loupe read from the forge: state, draft, checks, failedChecks, mergeability, review, readyToMerge and refreshedAt. Null when Loupe holds no reading.

agentReview.description: The agent review of the pull request, or null.

url.description: The review page of the document in the app.
The artifact page in the app.

siteReviewComments.description: The feedback items of the card: id, url (the Feedback tab at the note), pageUrl (the reviewed site page), surface, native, screenshot, anchors, body, hasDrawing, status, context and createdAt.

url.description: The card page in the app.

kind.description: How this card reads the other card.

url.description: The card page in the app.

requiresHumanReview.description: True when a person must review the pull request.

values.description: One row for each key the workflow template declares.

visibility.description: Who may write the key: any caller for public, only the workflow for internal.

value.description: The value of the key, or null when it is unset.

writer.description: Who last wrote the value: kind and name.

children.description: Empty for a type without the children capability.

url.description: The card page in the app.

progress.description: Null for a type without the children capability.

pause.description: The active workflow pause, or null.

state.description: What the card needs now on the board. Null for a card in a terminal column and a card with no mark.

others.description: The other reasons that apply, each with kind, code, reason and since.

PartialCardEvent.description: Some of the fields of `CardEvent`, each one whole. A field that the request does not name is absent.

name.description: The name of the person behind it, or null.

apiKey.description: The key that acted when `kind` is `api-key`, otherwise null.

from.description: The column a move left, with id, slug and label.

to.description: The column a move or a creation set, with id, slug and label.

cause.description: Why the app moved the card on its own, or null.

run.description: The whole record of a finished run, on a `run-finished` event.

pause.description: On a `paused` or `pause-released` event: kind, ruleId and releaseReason.

override.description: On a `review-overridden` or `override-ended` event: approver and headSha.

document.description: On a `document-verdict` or `verdict-failed` event: documentId, title, rule, verdict, withdrawn and refusal.

humanReview.description: On a `human-review-changed` event: value, cause and ruleId.

valueChange.description: On a `value-changed` event: key, value and previous.

PartialDocument.description: Some of the fields of `Document`, each one whole. A field that the request does not name is absent.

url.description: The review page of the document in the app, at the latest version.

markdown.description: The Markdown source of the current version.

references.description: The documents this one points at. Only this direction is writable.

referencedBy.description: The documents that point at this one.

PartialDocumentVersion.description: Some of the fields of `DocumentVersion`, each one whole. A field that the request does not name is absent.

threadCount.description: The number of comment threads on this version.

markdown.description: The Markdown source of this version.

PartialDocumentReview.description: Some of the fields of `DocumentReview`, each one whole. A field that the request does not name is absent.

verdict.description: The verdict standing on the current version. Null also after a withdrawal.

verdictId.description: The newest entry of the verdict log, a withdrawal included.

verdictThroughApiKey.description: An API key recorded the verdict for the owner.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before the next request.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The number of requests the window allows.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: The number of requests left in the window.

RateLimit-Reset.description: The seconds until the window resets.

Link.description: The next page, as `<url>; rel="next"`. It is absent on the last page.

Location.description: The URL of the new resource.

bearerAuth.description: An API key or an OAuth access token, in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
